gaps.title: Delete confirmation, recoverability and effect on shares
gaps.description: Delete is a confirmed management action (DEC-001) and appears as a per-row trash-icon button, but the Delete flow has no captured target. Whether deletion asks for confirmation, is permanent or recoverable, can be undone, and what happens to colleagues' existing viewer/editor access when a shared document is deleted is not shown in the capture and not answered by any decision.
gaps.why_it_matters: Every employee can delete their own documents in at most two clicks, and a deleted document may be one that colleagues currently view or edit, so a single misclick could remove work other people depend on.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Irreversible loss of documents, including shared ones, with no agreed recovery path; the two-click limit may be implemented in a way that leaves no safeguard.
research_questions: How do Google Drive and comparable document tools handle deletion of a shared document (trash, retention window, effect on collaborators' access)?
What do WCAG 2.2 success criterion 3.3.4 and established UX guidance recommend for confirming or reversing destructive actions?

gaps.title: What viewer and editor access each permit
gaps.description: Owners share with named colleagues as viewer or editor (DEC-005), and management is limited to employees' own documents (DEC-001). It is not stated what an editor may do beyond the owner's actions: edit content only, or also rename, delete, re-share or change others' access. It is also not stated whether a viewer may download or copy the document.
gaps.why_it_matters: Security is defined as only people the owner shares with can open a document (DEC-004); if editors can re-share, documents can reach people the owner never chose, and if editors can delete or rename they act on documents that are not their own, contrary to DEC-001.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The permission model cannot be specified; documents may be over-exposed or deleted by non-owners.

gaps.title: Whether the Documents list includes documents shared with the user
gaps.description: The captured Documents table shows Name and Modified columns and Share and Delete actions on the one row, with no owner or access-level column. It is not stated whether documents others have shared with the user appear in this list, separately, or not at all, and which actions are offered on a document the user does not own.
gaps.why_it_matters: A colleague given viewer or editor access needs some way to reach the shared document, and Share/Delete buttons on a non-owned row would contradict ownership-only management.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Shared colleagues may have no way to find documents, or may be shown actions they must not perform.

gaps.title: Rename not supported by any captured screen or action
gaps.description: Rename is a confirmed management action (DEC-001), but the inventory shows only Upload, Share and Delete; no rename control, inline edit or dialog is shown in the capture. Rules for renaming (allowed characters, length, handling of file extensions, clashes with an existing name) are not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Rename must be reachable within the two-click limit set in DEC-001, and nothing in the mockup shows where or how.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: A confirmed management action has no specified interaction or validation rules.
research_questions: What interaction patterns do established document tools such as Google Drive use for renaming a file from a list, and how do they handle extensions and name clashes?

gaps.title: Share flow not captured: choosing colleagues, roles and revoking
gaps.description: The Share button has no captured target. How an owner finds a named colleague, assigns viewer or editor, sees who currently has access, changes a role and revokes access (DEC-005) is not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: Sharing is the only route by which anyone other than the owner can open a document, so the owner must be able to see and correct who has access.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Revocation and access review cannot be specified, risking documents staying shared with the wrong people.
research_questions: How does Google Drive's share dialog let owners add named people, set viewer or editor, review current access and remove access?
Which accessibility considerations (WCAG 2.2 AA) apply to people-picker and role-selection controls in share dialogs?

gaps.title: Upload behaviour: types, sizes, failures and duplicate names
gaps.description: Upload is a confirmed action (DEC-001) but its flow has no captured target. Accepted file types, maximum size, multi-file upload, progress and confirmation, failure handling, retry after an interrupted upload, repeated submissions, and what happens when a document with the same name already exists are not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Upload is how documents enter the library; unclear limits and name-clash rules affect whether an existing document can be silently overwritten.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Upload cannot be specified or tested; duplicate or overwritten documents and unexplained failures are possible.
research_questions: How do Google Drive and similar tools handle uploading a file whose name matches an existing document (new version, renamed copy, or prompt)?
What are established patterns for showing upload progress, failure and retry for browser file uploads?

gaps.title: How the two-click limit is counted
gaps.description: DEC-001 says each of upload, rename, delete and share takes at most two clicks. It is not stated what counts as a click (for example, choosing a file in the system file picker, typing a new name or a colleague's name, confirming a deletion) or where counting starts.
gaps.why_it_matters: Sharing with a named colleague and a role, and any delete confirmation (GAP-001), may need more than two interactions, so the limit could conflict with other confirmed behaviour.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The ease criterion cannot be verified, and it may be met by dropping safeguards.

gaps.title: Listing up to 1,000 documents: sort, filter, search and pagination
gaps.description: REQ-005 requires pages to load within two seconds for up to 1,000 documents. The capture shows one row only; whether the list is sorted, filterable, searchable or paginated, and its default order, is not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: A must-have load target for 1,000 documents depends on how many rows a page shows, and finding one document among 1,000 bears on the 'easily' criterion.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The performance target cannot be tested against a defined page, and users may be unable to find documents.
research_questions: What sort, search and pagination conventions do document libraries such as Google Drive use for lists of around 1,000 items?
How is a two-second page load target usually measured (for example Largest Contentful Paint or time to interactive) for a list page?

gaps.title: Empty, loading, success and error states unobserved
gaps.description: Only a default state with one row was captured. What the Documents screen shows with no documents, while loading, and after an upload, rename, share or delete succeeds or fails is not shown in the capture.
gaps.checklist_item: Empty, loading, success and error states
gaps.why_it_matters: A new employee starts with an empty library, and each of the four management actions can fail; users need to know whether an action took effect.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: States will be designed ad hoc, and failed shares or deletes may go unnoticed.
research_questions: What do established design systems (for example GOV.UK Design System or Material Design) recommend for empty, loading and error states of a document list?
How should success and failure status messages be exposed to assistive technology under WCAG 2.2 success criterion 4.1.3?

gaps.title: Effect of revoking access while a colleague has the document open
gaps.description: Owners can revoke access at any time (DEC-005). What happens to a colleague who has the document open, or is mid-edit, when access is revoked or downgraded from editor to viewer is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: 'At any time' plus 'only people the owner shares with can open it' means revocation must take effect on users already viewing the document.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Revoked colleagues may keep access until they leave the page, and in-progress edits may be lost or saved without permission.
research_questions: How quickly does Google Drive apply revoked or downgraded access to a user who already has the document open, and what does that user see?

gaps.title: Ownership when an employee leaves or loses access
gaps.description: Management is limited to each employee's own documents and only shared people may open them. What happens to an employee's documents and their shares when the account is deactivated or the person leaves, and whether anyone can transfer ownership or recover them, is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: With owner-only control and no admin role mentioned, documents of a departed employee may become unmanageable or inaccessible to colleagues who rely on them.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Orphaned documents and no one able to correct sharing or deletion mistakes.

gaps.title: Icon-only Delete button and per-row action accessibility
gaps.description: Delete is shown as a trash icon in an unlabelled actions column. How the action is identified to sighted users without a text label, how each row's Share and Delete buttons are distinguished for screen-reader and keyboard users, and focus handling after a row is deleted are not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: With up to 1,000 rows, repeated 'Share' and 'Delete' buttons are indistinguishable without row context, increasing the chance of deleting the wrong document.
research_questions: Which WCAG 2.2 AA success criteria (for example 1.1.1, 2.4.6, 2.5.3, 4.1.2) apply to icon-only and repeated per-row action buttons in a data table?

gaps.title: Whether colleagues are notified of sharing or revocation
gaps.description: It is not stated whether a colleague is told when a document is shared with them, when their role changes, or when access is revoked, nor through which channel.
gaps.why_it_matters: Sharing with named colleagues is only useful if they learn of it; this links to how they find shared documents (GAP-003).
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Shared documents may go unnoticed, or notification scope is decided during build.

gaps.title: Concurrent actions by owner and editors
gaps.description: Owners and editors may act on the same document at once. What happens when an owner deletes or renames a document while an editor is editing it, or when two editors save at the same time, is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: The editor role introduces multiple writers to one document, and the list may show stale names or deleted documents.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Lost edits or errors when acting on a document that changed or no longer exists.
research_questions: How do document tools with viewer/editor sharing handle simultaneous edits and deletion of a document another user has open?

gaps.title: Meaning and format of 'Modified'
gaps.description: The table shows 'Modified' as a relative value ('2 days ago'). Which changes update it (content edit by an editor, rename, sharing change), whether it shows who modified, and how older dates and time zones are displayed are not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: With editors able to change shared documents, owners may rely on 'Modified' to notice others' changes.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Inconsistent timestamps and misleading change information.

assumptions.text: 'Named colleagues' in DEC-005 means other signed-in employees of the same organisation, so sharing is limited to people who can sign in.
assumptions.why: DEC-005 does not say whether colleagues outside the employee directory can be named.
assumptions.impact: Shapes the scope of GAP-002, GAP-005 and GAP-011.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm whether sharing is restricted to signed-in employees.

assumptions.text: The two-second target in REQ-005 applies to the Documents list page (SCR-001).
assumptions.impact: GAP-008 treats the list page as the page under test.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm which pages and which operations the target covers.

proposed_status_changes.reason: What viewer and editor access permit (re-share, rename, delete, download) is not stated; see GAP-002.
Delete recoverability and rename behaviour are not stated and not covered by the mockup; see GAP-001 and GAP-004.
